elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph says only "HDI shall indemnify the Company"; there is no "defend" (or "hold harmless") obligation and no reference to affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Indemnity runs to "the Company" only; affiliates are not covered.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: "any third-party claim alleging that the Site or the services provided by HDI under this Agreement infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: No breach-of-law trigger appears in the inserted language; the comment merely promises it as a preference.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No unauthorised access/disclosure of Company data trigger in the operative text.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: No gross negligence or wilful misconduct trigger in the operative text.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph contains no notice mechanic.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: No allocation of control of the defence or settlement is stated.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply adversely: the Agreement contains no Company indemnity (only the Section 7.2 advertising-content covenant, already scoped to Company-supplied content), so no broad Customer indemnity needs narrowing.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: "HDI shall indemnify the Company against any third-party claim alleging that the Site or the services provided by HDI ... infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: "except to the extent the claim arises from modifications made by the Company".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: "combination of the Site with items not supplied by HDI".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: "the Company's specifications or Content" — the specifications carve-out is present (the added "or Content" is an extra beyond the checklist).

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: "HDI shall procure for the Company the right to continue using the affected item, or modify or replace it so that it is non-infringing".

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: "if none of those remedies is reasonably available, HDI shall refund the fees paid by the Company for the affected item".

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: "shall not exceed three (3) times the fees paid or payable by the Company under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" — 3x a twelve-month (annual) fee base.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: Cap is expressed as a ceiling on HDI's liability under the indemnity paragraph, not as a reduction of any other Company right.

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: IP indemnity, the three customary exclusions, procure/modify/replace, refund, and a 3x twelve-month fee super-cap are all present in operative language.

Preferred level is not reached: no duty to defend, no affiliates, and no breach-of-law, Vendor-caused data breach, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct triggers, and no notice/control/cooperation procedure. These are only promised in the margin comment, which is not operative.

Minimality defect: the exclusion clause adds "or Content" alongside the Company's specifications. That is an extra, Customer-adverse carve-out outside the fallback checklist (which contemplates only modifications, combinations and specifications) and, in a hosting deal where the Company supplies the product content, it can swallow much of the indemnity. Delete "or Content" so the carve-out reads "...or the Company's specifications."

Drafting fix (non-fatal): the inserted paragraph is unnumbered but its cap sentence refers to "this Section 9.1", while Section 9 is lettered (a)/(b). Number the insertion consistently (e.g. "9(c)" or a new Section 10) and conform the internal reference so the cap's scope is unambiguous.
Intent is otherwise preserved: Sections 9(a) and 9(b), including the Globix carve-out, are retained verbatim and nothing in the insertion contradicts existing allocation, remedies or timing.
